subject: Food Science
title: Glass vs. Plastic vs. Metal
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Glass vs. Plastic vs. Metal.

hook.text: Coca-Cola tastes different from a glass bottle, aluminum can, and plastic bottle—even though the formula is identical.

buildup.text: Glass is chemically inert—zero interaction with food. Metal can impart metallic taste.

discovery.text: Glass lets zero oxygen through. Plastic allows slow oxygen permeation. That's why beer in green or brown glass bottles lasts.

twist.text: Aluminum cans are lined with polymer to prevent metal contact. Without it, acidic beverages like soda would corrode through.

climax.text: Glass is infinitely recyclable without quality loss. Plastic degrades each cycle.

punchline.text: Glass is inert but heavy. Metal is light but reactive. Plastic is cheap but permeable.

quiz.question: Why do aluminum cans need polymer linings inside?
options: Without lining, acidic beverages would corrode through the aluminum in days
